newsitem.title: INDIA: SONIA GANDHI ELECTRIFIES INDIA'S CONGRESS PARTY.
newsitem.headline: SONIA GANDHI ELECTRIFIES INDIA'S CONGRESS PARTY.

text.p: The reclusive widow of Rajiv Gandhi on Saturday roused a brooding Congress party, breaking her silence to urge India's oldest political grouping to rededicate itself to the nation's teeming masses.
Thousands of frenzied Congress activists erupted in a demonstration of support for the Italian-born Sonia Gandhi when she appeared at a party convention in the eastern city of Calcutta.
Excited party activists shouted, stamped and applauded when the inheritor of the Nehru-Gandhi mantle entered the stadium on the second day of the party's three-day meeting.
"Long Live Sonia Gandhi! Long Live Rajiv Gandhi! Long Live Indira Gandhi!" they shouted for 10 minutes as Sonia Gandhi, 50, waved before taking a seat below the stage.
It was the moment the delegates had been waiting for after Congress's humiliating defeat in general elections last year and 16 months in the political wilderness.
As soon as party president Sitaram Kesri began his speech, the crowd of about 10,000 clamoured for Sonia Gandhi to be brought to the dais, preventing Kesri from speaking.
After five minutes of din, the party president stepped off the platform and led Sonia Gandhi on to the stage, where she took a seat.
Later the woman who usually wields power from her drawing room, not the political stump, briefly addressed the crowd.
"I'm not here to give a speech but I will say a few words," she said in English, then Hindi.

"In 1985, my husband had raised a few questions which we should consider seriously," she said before reading from a 1985 speech by her husband, who was prime minister from 1984 to 1989 and was killed by a suicide bomber while campaigning in 1991.
Her words were drowned in cheers and slogans.
In the speech, Rajiv Gandhi said Congress had lost touch with the masses and urged the nation's oldest party to recommit itself.

"Today, on the auspicious 80th plenary session of the Indian National Congress and on the 50th anniversary of independence, let us all, Congressmen and women, rededicate ourselves to this task," Sonia Gandhi said.
Congress has led India for all but five of its 50 years since independence, with Rajiv Gandhi, his mother Indira Gandhi and her father Jawaharlal Nehru together ruling for 38 years.
The outpouring of support underscored the popularity of Sonia Gandhi, who has played a behind-the-scenes role in party politics since her husband's murder.
But in May she formally joined Congress, stirring speculation that she was prepared to assume a leadership role.

The Congress president relished the appearance of Sonia Gandhi, who many party members are hoping will lead the party back into power. Currently it supports the centre-left ruling coalition but holds no government portfolios.
"We were delinked from the Gandhi-Nehru family, but we are once again proud of being linked to it," Kesri said to thunderous clapping.
"Soniaji, do whatever you feel, but don't break the link with Congress," he said, using a form of respect to address the party's darling. "You are a source of strength and inspiration to Congress."
